## Evidence Review — Chapter 5B (Economic Wellbeing)

| evidence_id | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| EF-E4db2bc261eb4 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt fully supports: 8.5% nominal expenditure increase, non-contributory elderly pensions, priority infrastructure, fertilizers, national milk, rural supplies, no tax code change, continued anti-evasion. |
| EF-Eb5e5fcb3575a | **REJECT** | Excerpt is truncated to a budget-table fragment ending mid-sentence. It does not contain the claimed growth deceleration figures (2.1% → 1.2%), a weakening domestic/U.S. demand outlook, or any reference to staff projections. The excerpt ends at the pension line. Claim cannot be verified from this excerpt. |
| EF-E9e3b0020ff59 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms Banxico escalating from 25 bp → 50 bp → 75 bp as inflation broadened, policy rate at 9.25%, ~6 pp above U.S. Fed. |
| EF-E9c850e9c3f11 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms markets pricing terminal rate ~10.5% in Q1 2023. "No indication of political loyalty-driven retention" is a negative inference drawn from market pricing; the excerpt itself does not assert independence but is consistent with that reading. |
| EF-E3bdfe881eb44 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms peso broadly stable, rising interest differential, strong fiscal fundamentals, Banxico commitment to price stability, solid remittances, reserves adequate at 125% of ARA. |
| EF-Ea4106b5c2163 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms deficit increase 3.8→4.1% of GDP, driven by interest payments, staff estimating neutral fiscal stance in 2023. |
| EF-Eefb097f1033b | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms fuel pricing regime cost rose post-Ukraine invasion, higher-than-budgeted subsidies in 2022H1, budget zeroing out fuel subsidy for 2023. |
| EF-E1562b2d6859f | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms FX loans at nominal pre-pandemic levels, peso-denominated loans recovering after a year of stagnation, corporates entering tightening with healthy buffers (smaller than a decade ago). |
| EF-E0e7da66c8a2b | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms capital adequacy ratio over 19%, up from 16% pre-pandemic, large institutions holding ample liquidity buffers. |
| EF-E0b9146d90be4 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms nonbinding agreement with food producers/distributors on 24 items for six months, temporary tariff reductions, steps to reduce distribution costs and promote food production for small farmers. |
| EF-Ed1f93dcb8c1a | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms 8.5% nominal expenditure increase, accommodating interest payments, non-contributory elderly pensions, priority infrastructure, fertilizers, milk, rural supplies (modest size confirmed). |
| EF-E79b6093492a5 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms 2021 ROSC found national accounts high quality, Mexico subscribes to SDDS, improvement areas: chained volume indices, goods processing abroad, illegal activities coverage, accrual vs. cash government recording. |
| EF-E6ac9086d452e | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms ROSC identified need for greater consistency between Banxico and SHCP data recording and regular reconciliation exercises for public sector discrepancies. |
| EF-E3763e722bd87 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms Mexico reports 14 core + 9 encouraged indicators for deposit takers, 2 OFC, 1 household, 1 real estate FSIs; reporting interrupted after May 2021 for IFRS 9 revision, expected resumption end-2022. |
| EF-E9bd8e66284f8 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms increased allotments for fertilizers, milk, rural supplies targeted at small farmers/rural populations, non-contributory elderly pensions maintained, no tax code change, anti-evasion efforts (not base-broadening reform). |
| EF-E634d0e6f8f49 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms Russia-Ukraine-driven fuel subsidy overrun in 2022H1, nonbinding agreement on 24 items for six months, temporary tariff reductions, distribution cost reduction and domestic food production promotion for small farmers. |
| EF-E664aa6470252 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms progressive Banxico tightening escalation (25→50→75 bp), policy rate 9.25%, 6 pp above U.S. Fed, terminal rate ~10.5% in Q1 2023. |
| EF-E5d20cbe307c1 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms PEMEX EBITDA over USD 23 billion in 2022H1 (more than doubled), reflecting higher oil prices and modest production increase; cash generation rise allocated mostly to debt amortization; debt remains high with spreads exceeding government bonds and most peers. |
| EF-E17e53c84ca26 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms moderate portfolio outflows from nonresident peso-bond sales, offset by domestic institutional (pension fund) buying, reserves adequate at 125% of ARA despite declining from August 2021 SDR peak, peso stable on interest differential/fiscal fundamentals/monetary commitment/remittances. |
| EF-Ea7a27730304b | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt confirms capital adequacy over 19% (up from 16% pre-pandemic), large institutions with ample liquidity, credit growth recovering with FX and peso loans reaching/near pre-pandemic nominal levels, corporates with healthy buffers (smaller than a decade ago). |

**Summary:** 1 rejection, 19 acceptances. The single rejection (EF-Eb5e5fcb3575a) is due to an excerpt truncation that omits the growth projection data needed to verify the claim; the underlying source may support it but the cited passage does not.
